issue.title: Make @TestSecurity work correctly with unannotated JAX-RS endpoints security feature
issue.body:
The use of `quarkus.security.jaxrs.deny-unannotated-endpoints=true` essentially
results in the addition of a `DenyAllInterceptor` to the invocation chain
of a JAX-RS endpoint.
Because this interceptor did not take into account the `AuthorizationController`
(like the `RolesAllowedInterceptor` already does), it would result in endpoints
being secured even though security was supposed to be disabled for the specific test.

Fixes: #19896

issue.title: `@TestSecurity(authorizationEnabled = false)` does not work with `quarkus.security.jaxrs.deny-unannotated-endpoints`

labels.name: triage/duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

issue.body:
## Describe the bug
When an application sets `quarkus.security.jaxrs.deny-unannotated-endpoints` to `true` then a test annotated with `@TestSecurity(authorizationEnabled = false)` will get a `401` rather than a `200` status when calling an endpoint annotated with `@RolesAllowed`. This in contrast to when `quarkus.security.jaxrs.deny-unannotated-endpoints` is not set (to `true`).

### Expected behavior
Even when `quarkus.security.jaxrs.deny-unannotated-endpoints` is set to `true` I would expect `@TestSecurity(authorizationEnabled = false)` annotated tests to pass.

### Actual behavior
A test like the following will fail, because the returned status is 401 rather than 200:
```java
    @Test
    @TestSecurity(authorizationEnabled = false)
    void authorizationDisabled() {
        Assertions.assertEquals(200, RestAssured.get().thenReturn().statusCode());
    }
```

By also declaring the `user` and `roles` the test can be made to pass:
```java
    @Test
    @TestSecurity(authorizationEnabled = false, user = "foo", roles = "user")
    void authorizationDisabled() {
        Assertions.assertEquals(200, RestAssured.get().thenReturn().statusCode());
    }
```

## To Reproduce
1. Clone https://github.com/knutwannheden/test-disable-authorization
2. Run `mvn verify`
3. The test `DenyUnannotatedTest#authorizationDisabled()` fails while `StandardTest#authorizationDisabled()` passes. The former has `quarkus.security.jaxrs.deny-unannotated-endpoints` set to `true`.

### Configuration
```properties
quarkus.security.jaxrs.deny-unannotated-endpoints=true
```
